text:
maria_sales: Quick heads-up — new POC with FinSys (regulated payments). They want Private deployment in their AWS account and asked for network checklist + cost implications. Can we align on recommended connectivity options?

aaron_se: Thanks Maria. Main asks from them: 1) minimal blast radius (can't route production traffic through our VPC), 2) predictable egress cost estimate, 3) allowlist IPs + firewall rules for outbound.

sanjay_neteng: For Private (customer VPC) we usually recommend one of: VPC peering for simple low-latency, or PrivateLink (interface endpoints) for tighter isolation. Transit Gateway if multiple VPCs. Their constraint about not routing prod through our VPC favors PrivateLink.

maria_sales: @sanjay noted PrivateLink. Customer also asked whether PrivateLink requires NAT or changes their egress path. They use a strict egress proxy and have multiple availability zones.

sanjay_neteng: PrivateLink terminates on eni in their VPC, traffic stays in their VPC/subnets to reach the endpoint. Outbound egress from the model hosts -> customer backends depends on routing. If they want our service to call back to an on-prem IP, that's separate. PrivateLink itself does not force internet egress via NAT.

julia_solutions: Practical checklist I give customers:
- Create a dedicated subnet for interface endpoints (no IGW)
- Security groups on endpoints allow only our control-plane IPs (we'll publish IPs)
- Route table: local routes only, no peering routes unless they opt-in
- Egress proxy: ensure outbound 443 allowed from model hosts to your services

maria_sales: They asked for concrete firewall/SG lines we can paste into their security team questionnaire. Can we draft minimal rules?

sanjay_neteng: Draft SG rules (customer side) — allow inbound from endpoint ENIs (we'll provide CIDR range) and allow outbound to our control plane for healthchecks. Example:```
# customer-security-group (attached to endpoint subnets)
Inbound:
- Type: HTTPS (TCP 443) Source: sg:endpoint-eni
- Type: Custom TCP (port 1024-65535) Source: sg:endpoint-eni  # optional ephemeral
Outbound:
- Type: HTTPS (TCP 443) Destination: 0.0.0.0/0  # if egress proxy, lock to proxy IP
- Type: Healthcheck (TCP 8080) Destination: 10.0.5.12/32  # example internal monitoring
```

aaron_se: Also need to call out NAT/GW cost scenarios: if they route traffic from model hosts to the internet (e.g., to call external APIs during inference), they'll incur NAT gateway hours + bytes. If they put an egress proxy in their VPC, costs move to their side and are easier to forecast. We should provide example numbers for 1M requests/month.

julia_solutions: Agreed. Quick calc to show impact: sample traffic pattern: average 5 tokens per request, ~1KB per request egress. 1M requests -> ~1GB egress (low) but TLS + retransmits bump it. NAT Gateway data transfer pricing can add up if they expect heavy model-driven external calls. Recommend: keep third-party calls inside VPC or use VPC endpoints for those services.

maria_sales: They also asked about IP allowlist for our managed control-plane when we need to push model updates to the dedicated hosts. Can we provide a pinned set or a stable CIDR?

sanjay_neteng: We publish a small set of egress CIDR ranges per-region for control-plane operations. We can provide a /24 per region as an allowlist for the POC (temporary). For production we'll suggest a more robust approach: mutual TLS + service auth so IP spoofing isn't a single point of failure.

maria_sales: Great. Any blockers on using Transit Gateway instead? They said they might connect multiple accounts and prefer centralized routing.

sanjay_neteng: TGW works well for multi-account topologies but forces you to manage route propagation and can expose more network surface area. For regulated workloads PrivateLink avoids routing between VPCs and is simpler to certify. If they need hub-and-spoke, TGW + route filters is fine.

julia_solutions: One more POC tip: enable our prefix caching feature (saves repeated egress to identical destinations) — ask them to share top external hosts list so we can advise on endpoints to pin in their VPC.

maria_sales: OK I'll assemble a one-pager: recommended topology (Privatelink + endpoint subnets), SG snippets, allowlist CIDRs, and a cost note on NAT vs egress-proxy. Who can review before I send?

aaron_se: I'll review security copy. @sanjay please verify the SG snippet and the CIDR /24 per region we plan to hand off.

sanjay_neteng: Will do. Also ping infra-bot to attach the control-plane CIDR doc.

infra-bot: Attached: https://redwood.internal/infra/control-plane-egress-cidrs/v1.csv (automated update) :robot_face:

maria_sales: Thanks all — target to send to customer tomorrow EOD. I'll post draft here shortly for final sign-off. :thumbsup:
